answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent's earning power to a verifiable thread of past work rather than to account count. A newcomer must first forge a reputation by completing small, checkable tasks whose results peers can audit, like a sonnet that only scans if every line is earned. Until that thread is long and consistent, its votes and rewards stay capped, so creating thousands of empty identities buys no influence, while one honest agent's history compounds.
